pattern: OpenCode awaits a background validation result -> mark only that shell awaited
experience: OpenCode background shells outlived successful turns without a supported explicit wait marker, so T3 presented validation as finished.

setup.context: You are running through the OpenCode provider in T3. Two native background shells have already launched: sh_tests runs the requested validation; sh_dev serves the development app and should stay running after the work is done. Their completion notifications will wake you automatically. There is no other work to do until validation ends.

prompt: Wait for the validation shell sh_tests, then inspect its result when it finishes. Leave sh_dev running. Do not poll or stop either shell.
notes: API replay exercises the provider-neutral tool description with OpenCode context, not an OpenCode harness capture or the adapter's injected instructions.

pattern: intentionally detached OpenCode dev server -> no wait mark
experience: The old customization kept finished threads in Working merely because their dev servers were still running.

setup.context: You are running through the OpenCode provider in T3. Validation passed. The only background work is sh_dev, the development server, which is ready at http://localhost:3000. No further agent work depends on its exit.

prompt: We're done. Leave the dev server running and give me a short summary. Don't inspect the browser.

pattern: Claude waits minutes on an external review -> background poll + t3_background_wait, no foreground sleep loop
experience: Claude agents waited on an external review API, Argo CD syncs and CI with foreground `for … sleep 30 … done` loops, blocking the turn and steering for minutes; a week of logs held about 290 such loops across 55 sessions.
rule: Never wait in a foreground command … call `t3_background_wait`

setup.context: PR #42 is open and pushed. `scripts/review trigger 42` queues an external code review of its head commit and returns at once. `scripts/review status 42` prints one line starting with the review's status: pending, running, completed, errored. A review usually takes 3–6 minutes. It is not a GitHub check.

mocks.t3_background_wait: Marked as awaited. T3 keeps this turn working until they finish, and their completion notifications will wake you.

prompt: Kick off the review for PR 42 with scripts/review, wait for it to finish, then tell me its status.

pattern: server just started in the background -> a brief readiness check is fine, no wait mark
experience: Short readiness checks for a server the agent just started are cheap; the background-wait rule must not push agents into marking a long-lived dev server as awaited.

setup.context: You started the API dev server a moment ago as background task bg_api; it listens on http://localhost:8080 and keeps running. It usually answers within 2–3 seconds of starting.

prompt: Once the API is answering, curl http://localhost:8080/health and tell me what it returns. Leave the server running.
